title: Training-only product-key addressing for bounded persistent-state retrieval
question: Can factorized product-key addressing preserve the fixed cosine teacher's target retrieval while restricting the fine reranker to K=4,8,16 states?
hypothesis: Factorizing the fixed width-16 representation into two training-fitted codebooks may provide higher coarse target retention than the learned prototype proposal at comparable bounded shortlist budgets.

arms.name: exhaustive_cosine
arms.intervention: cosine-score all 64 persistent states with the fixed width-16 teacher representation

arms.name: product_key
arms.intervention: training-only two-factor product-key cell proposal followed by the same fixed cosine reranker

decision_rule.condition: report proposal retention, actual target recall, end-to-end success, state candidates scored, and total arithmetic separately for K=4,8,16
decision_rule.licenses: diagnostic evidence about training-only product-key addressing on the registered workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal product-key retrieval guarantees or hardware wall-clock speedup

decision_rule.condition: actual target recall and end-to-end success approach the exhaustive cosine reference while retained states and arithmetic remain bounded
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support for the product-key sparse retrieval mechanism on this workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: broad C5 or general semantic memory claims

held_constant: 48 training semantic codes versus 16 held-out query codes
all 64 runtime persistent states are assigned to the learned product-key cells
same K budgets and beam mapping as the sparse-funnel diagnostic
arithmetic is reported separately from wall-clock behavior
result_note: Full registered run 36699321108: pooled K=16 actual target recall 0.6240 and end-to-end success 0.7980 versus exhaustive 0.7000 and 0.8333. Artifact 11089197442, digest sha256:f0ed3bea00e2ef71b17234db16244f1d475e7567079a2af30b036c185c07c0d1.
